theme: Indus and western archaeological weight metrology
question: How closely do complete catalogue weights fit declared Indus/local series, and how does fit vary by site, class, material, shape, preservation and context?
outcome: Extracted 2,058 unique entries including 938 Greater Indus records. A 60-entry author page audit found five period-field errors before repair and no observed mass/+x errors. The 298 intact certain Dholavira objects give unit 14.0029006 g (bootstrap 13.8193732–14.5178200), signal CV 4.32134% (2.41069–15.84863). Among 701 eligible western records, 136 prefer the Indus reference geometrically; 18 meet <=3% and >=1 percentage-point advantage (2.56776%, Wilson 1.63030–4.02224%). A seven-object Gulf supplement is Exploratory. Eighteen numerical files and nine local derivatives reproduced byte for byte.
challenge: Source classification/context arithmetic disagrees with simple field counts; material/period and denomination assumptions are confounded. Several full-text precedents remain unavailable. Site-derived Monte Carlo seeds differ from the protocol's single named seed. Catalogue fit does not identify object origin or manufacturing error separately.
remedy: Preserved all earlier extraction/analysis witnesses; recorded source page audit and class discrepancy; used a background mixture, declared supports, damage selections, strata and sensitivity frames. Excluded prior Susa accession collisions. Annotated seed deviations and post-endpoint Gulf comparison as Exploratory. Independently verified arithmetic and repeated the full computation.
retry_when: Independent reweighing and wear documentation, reconciled DHR contexts/classes, recovered original precedent chapters, complete Gulf assemblages or historically justified additional levels/denomination-frequency models provide new evidence. Any changed model or common-seed control needs a new dated protocol and endpoint.
